sub_questions.question: Can I use our existing Azure OpenAI deployment instead of regular OpenAI as a model provider?

claims.claim: Azure OpenAI cannot be used with Dify (answer: 'Unfortunately not').
claims.guide_evidence: OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, and others are published officially

claims.claim: Dify connects to the standard OpenAI API only.
claims.guide_evidence: Install the plugin for the desired provider (OpenAI, Anthropic, Azure OpenAI, and others are published officially; additional community providers are also listed).

claims.claim: An Azure OpenAI deployment can't be added as a model provider.
claims.guide_evidence: for Azure OpenAI, also the resource endpoint URL and deployment name.

claims.claim: The customer would need to use a regular OpenAI API key instead.
claims.guide_evidence: Enter the credentials the provider requires — typically an API key, and for Azure OpenAI, also the resource endpoint URL and deployment name.

evaluation.rationale: The guide says Azure OpenAI is an officially published model-provider plugin and explains how to set it up (API key, resource endpoint URL and deployment name under Settings → Model Provider). The answer flatly denies this and tells Tom to get a regular OpenAI key instead. He would plausibly act on that by dropping his existing Azure deployment and paying for a separate provider account.
